title: Global Internal Audit & Advisory Director
description:
TransUnion's Job Applicant Privacy Notice Personal Information We Collect Your Privacy Choices Team Overview Global Audit & Advisory (GAA) is an independent and objective assurance and advisory function focused on adding value and improving TransUnion’s operations through a systematic and disciplined approach to evaluating governance, risk management, and internal control processes. The team partners with business and functional leadership globally to provide relevant insights and recommendations that strengthen organizational effectiveness and efficiency. This role reports to the VP, Global Audit & Advisory.

This is a hybrid position and involves regular performance of job responsibilities virtually as well as in-person at an assigned TU office location for a minimum of two days a week. Role Overview and Core Responsibilities Lead GAA’s global professional practices function and provide leadership oversight for designated international audit regions, ensuring consistent, risk-based, and value-focused execution of assurance and advisory activities. Own and continuously enhance GAA’s audit methodology, audit manual, templates, guidance, documentation standards, issue management practices, and quality expectations in alignment with the Global Internal Audit Standards and applicable regulatory expectations. Lead the Quality Assurance and Improvement Program (QAIP), including ongoing monitoring, internal assessments, external quality assessment readiness, and remediation of identified improvement opportunities. Lead or coordinate the global risk assessment and annual audit planning methodology, including maintenance of the audit universe, integration with enterprise risk information, prioritization of emerging risks, and monitoring of audit plan delivery, coverage, resources, and capacity. Support executive and Audit Committee reporting on audit plan performance, significant themes, open issues, quality measures, resource capacity, and emerging risks, while providing clear and actionable insights to senior leadership. Develop and advance GAA’s audit technology, data analytics, automation, and artificial intelligence strategy, embedding responsible use of these capabilities throughout planning, fieldwork, reporting, knowledge management, and continuous monitoring while maintaining appropriate human judgment and accountability. Provide leadership oversight for designated international audit regions, monitoring portfolio execution, audit quality, stakeholder relationships, regulatory considerations, resources, and issue escalation while aligning regional priorities with the overall global audit strategy. Lead selected cross-border, enterprise-wide, and strategically significant assurance and advisory engagements while partnering with regional audit leaders, business and functional stakeholders, external auditors, regulators, and other assurance providers. Lead and support GAA talent and capability development through competency frameworks, learning strategies, coaching, knowledge sharing, succession planning, professional certification, and development of regional leaders and engagement teams. Serve as a trusted advisor and change leader, providing pragmatic, risk-based guidance to senior stakeholders and partnering with GAA leadership on strategic initiatives that strengthen governance, controls, audit quality, innovation, and organizational effectiveness. Required Knowledge and Experiences 12 or more years of progressively responsible internal audit experience, including leadership of complex or geographically dispersed teams; professional practices experience is highly preferred. Demonstrated expertise in internal audit methodology, risk assessment, audit planning, quality assurance, issue management, executive reporting, and the Global Internal Audit Standards, including experience preparing for or leading internal and external quality assessments. Experience leading global or cross-regional audit initiatives and operating effectively across different regulatory, cultural, and business environments, with the executive presence and judgment to constructively challenge and influence senior stakeholders. Demonstrated experience developing leaders and teams, managing organizational change, and building trusted relationships across business functions, regions, external auditors, regulators, and other assurance providers. Professional certification such as Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA), Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE), or equivalent is strongly preferred; experience within financial services, consumer data, technology, privacy, regulatory, or compliance environments is beneficial. Required Technical Skills Advanced knowledge and practical application of the Global Internal Audit Standards, internal audit methodologies, risk assessment, audit planning, quality assurance, and issue management frameworks. title: Manager, Technical & Operational Accounting
description: About the Team OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission. The Technical Accounting, Accounting Policy, and Financial Reporting organization partners across Finance to assess complex corporate matters and develop well-supported U.S. GAAP conclusions. The team supports non-routine business activities requiring thoughtful technical judgment, scalable accounting policies, financial statement disclosures, processes, and controls. About the Role You will partner closely with Technical Accounting, Financial Reporting and Controllership to translate complex accounting conclusions into scalable operational procedures. You will build processes for non-standard transactions, including warrants, equity-method investments, debt and equity securities, non-controlling interests, hypothetical liquidation at book value allocations, business combinations, and other complex financing, investment, and capital arrangements. You will advise stakeholders across Corporate Accounting, Financial Reporting, Treasury, Legal, Tax, Strategic Finance, FP&A, Equity, Internal Controls, valuation specialists, and external auditors. You will help resolve complex accounting questions, align leaders on material judgments and risks, and translate conclusions into audit-ready memoranda, close entries, disclosures, processes, and controls. This is a highly visible role for an accounting professional who can turn technical conclusions into practical execution, support non-routine transactions through recurring close processes, and strengthen operational accounting across Finance. In this role, you will: - Own operational accounting for complex financing, investment, equity, and capital arrangements, including classification, measurement, presentation, disclosure, and recurring close processes. - In partnership with technical accounting, lead day-one and recurring accounting for non-standard transactions, including fair-value measurements, equity-method investments, debt and equity securities, warrants, noncontrolling interests, and hypothetical liquidation at book value allocations. - Perform reconciliations for assigned accounts, investigate discrepancies, and drive issues to resolution. - Support the resolution of complex accounting matters during monthly and quarterly close. Ensure conclusions are reflected in financial statement presentation, footnote disclosures, journal entries, reconciliations, ownership, and controls. - Build operational processes to assess impairment indicators and asset recoverability for goodwill, intangible assets, long-lived asset groups, equity-method investments, nonmarketable equity investments, and debt securities, as applicable. - Coordinate valuations for non-standard transactions with Technical Accounting and valuation specialists. - Lead audit support for assigned investments and other complex accounting areas. Prepare evidence-backed schedules, memoranda, reconciliations, valuation support, and financial statement tie-outs. - Analyze significant equity and other compensation awards, and partner with Equity Administration and Controllership to ensure accurate, timely accounting and booking. - Coordinate with Tax on downstream impacts without owning tax conclusions. - Partner with Financial Reporting and Internal Controls to strengthen controls, SOX/ICFR readiness, impairment monitoring, audit trails, tie-outs, and subsequent-event procedures. - Monitor emerging accounting standards and translate new guidance into policies, implementation plans, disclosures, reporting calendars, and scalable processes. - Participate in cross-functional initiatives involving accounting-policy implementation, operating-model changes, legal-entity matters, and systems or process improvements. - Develop pragmatic accounting policies, playbooks, decision frameworks, and automation that improve consistency, strengthen capability, preserve judgment, reflect economic substance, and escalate unresolved issues. You might thrive in this role if you: - Hold a CPA, CA, or equivalent accounting qualification, or bring comparable demonstrated technical-accounting expertise. - Bring 5+ years of progressive experience in technical accounting, accounting advisory, public accounting, corporate controllership, or complex financial reporting, with meaningful industry or transaction experience. - Demonstrate broad U.S. GAAP expertise across corporate accounting, financial instruments, consolidation, business combinations, equity-method investments, debt and equity securities, impairment, fair value, financial statement presentation, and complex ownership structures. - Apply relevant guidance across ASC 320, 321, 323 326, 350, 360, 470, 480, 718, 805, 810, 815, and 820; and other applicable guidance as the facts require. - Have developed or reviewed audit-ready technical memoranda, implemented conclusions in recurring operations, worked constructively with external auditors, and ground

The role evaluates the quality of audit execution, risk coverage, and the support for key audit judgments and conclusions, and provides objective, effective challenge to identify gaps and opportunities to strengthen audit quality. title: Capital Markets, Senior Compliance Officer
description: Application Deadline: 10/30/2026 Address: 151 W 42nd Street Job Family Group: Audit, Risk & Compliance The Capital Markets Senior Compliance Officer will assist in the effective implementation, maintenance and administration of the Capital Markets Compliance Program. The role provides compliance advisory services, coordinates and performs ongoing risk assessment, monitoring and surveillance activities to ensure that the Compliance Program remains current and aligned with the Firm’s Enterprise-wide Compliance Program. The role works closely with the relevant other internal business partners to ensure regulatory, corporate and fiduciary obligations are met. This role will have a specific focus on compliance oversight over BMO’s Capital Markets and equity activities. The Capital Markets Senior Compliance Officer maintains current knowledge of regulatory requirements and developments, monitors risk, identifies and corrects possible gaps and weaknesses. This individual will be responsible for the successful implementation and maintenance of the Firm’s compliance framework. This role provides real-time guidance to Capital Markets management on implications of new regulatory policies or Bank products and assists in the implementation of new or revised policies and programs to address them. The role develops and maintains compliance information for analysis and reporting. Conduct surveillance reviews and evaluate accuracy, reliability and integrity of the compliance analytics and findings produced. Identify potential issues associated with surveillance tools and process enhancements and development scenarios. Communicate and escalate potential issues for timely addressing and resolution. Fortify detection capabilities and innovation within the program. Respond to inquiries from auditors and regulators; participate in initiatives to drive adherence to regulatory frameworks and documentation. In coordination with the CCO, support the CMC equity program including a focus on building and executing the monitoring framework and compliance responsibilities Assist in the development of the Equity Compliance Program regarding FINRA broker-dealer requirements and corresponding oversight. Execute appropriate testing and analyze key performance indicators to ensure requirements of the LOB policies and programs are maintained at a level commensurate with regulatory expectations. Support root cause analysis in response to material control failures in line(s) of business. Review electronic communications. Analyze and explore multiple data types in order to identify anomalies and patterns of risk Anticipate potential consequences of unaddressed risk factors or shortfalls in compliance and recommend appropriate controls. Monitor and assess regulatory developments impacting equities businesses and assist with updating policies and procedures as needed. Participate in risk assessments , issue tracking, and remediation efforts to address control gaps and regulatory findings. Leverages feedback to improve processes collaborating with leadership teams across departments. Must be a highly motivated candidate with the ability to work independently. title: Credit Risk Review - Strategic Insight Team Manager
description: Location: For Those Who Work At Home, Ohio POSITION OVERVIEW Credit Risk Review (CRR) operates as an independent Second Line of Defense function that provides objective assessment of credit risk and credit risk management practices. CRR performs ongoing credit reviews, validates risk ratings and credit quality, identifies emerging portfolio risks, and provides timely insights to management and the Risk Committee. The Strategic Insights Team (SIT) Manager is the integrative leadership role responsible for converting CRR’s mandate and priorities into a sustainable operating model. The Manager leads a multidisciplinary team spanning strategy, quality, business operations and administration, technology and AI enablement, and data and reporting. The role has enterprise accountability for CRR planning, execution infrastructure, tools, quality, governance, reporting, regulatory readiness, and continuous improvement. The Manager serves as a strategic extension of the Head of CRR and a primary connection point across CRR leadership, review teams, senior risk management, the Board, regulators, Internal Audit, external reviewers, and enterprise partners. Success requires strong credit-risk judgment, sustained leadership presence, organization, creative problem-solving, and the ability to lead multiple interdependent workstreams while anticipating downstream impacts. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS Enterprise leadership and operating model. Lead the design and continuous evolution of CRR’s operating model, governance, organizational responsibilities, management routines, processes, tools, and supporting infrastructure. Create structure in ambiguous or evolving areas and identify gaps before they become execution failures. Strategy and transformation execution. Establish CRR’s strategic agenda and translate priorities into coordinated initiatives, milestones, ownership, dependencies, communications, and measurable outcomes. Lead multiple concurrent workstreams as project sponsor, project leader, design authority, or escalation point. Annual planning, risk assessment, and capacity. Lead strategic planning, annual risk-based coverage planning, risk-assessment recalibration, capacity analysis, staffing scenarios, and prioritization. Connect portfolio risk, Risk Intelligence, cycle requirements, quality needs, resource constraints, and emerging workload to defensible coverage and staffing recommendations. Execution and KPI accountability. Own CRR’s performance-management infrastructure, including KPI design, definitions, data integrity, thresholds, governance, reporting, and escalation. Monitor execution against review plans, coverage, timelines, quality expectations, talent measures, and strategic commitments; drive corrective action when risks or conflicts emerge. Credit-risk and review judgment. Apply strong knowledge of commercial and consumer credit, portfolio management, risk ratings, underwriting, ongoing monitoring, problem-credit management, sampling, and credit review practices. Assess how policy, portfolio, economic, data, system, or methodology changes affect CRR scope, tools, staffing, testing, and reporting. Risk Intelligence, data, and executive reporting. Lead CRR’s Risk Intelligence, ongoing monitoring, red-flag, analytics, dashboard, and management-reporting capabilities. Integrate portfolio trends, review results, quality themes, internal indicators, and external developments into forward-looking insights, testing direction, planning decisions, and concise executive, regulatory, and Board reporting. Technology, automation, and AI enablement. Serve as business sponsor and product owner for CRR tools and data solutions from concept and requirements through testing, implementation, adoption, guidance, maintenance, and enhancement. Governance, GRC, controls, and issues management. title: Compliance Manager, User Enablement
description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies — from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups — use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team Stripe's Financial Crimes, Compliance and Risk Oversight (FinCRO) organisation serves as Stripe's second line of defense, ensuring we operate as a responsible steward of the global financial ecosystem. You will join the Product and User Enablement (ProUse) team within FinCRO, acting as a trusted compliance advisor to our first line business teams (e.g., GTM, Risk, Ops) to help scale business and grow our user base globally.  What you’ll do We are looking for an experienced compliance advisor who is fluent in both compliance regulations and commercial reality. You will not just be a specialized advisor, but a strategic partner responsible for scaling our business by embedding compliance intelligence directly into our technical infrastructure to support our users. You will be the bridge between Stripe’s compliance obligations and our users' ambitious goals, moving away from manual, person-dependent models toward a dynamic, agentic structure. You will provide expert guidance for our complex user challenges to actively shape them. You will partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders to design user solutions that both support users' growing journey with Stripe and satisfy compliance rigor. Stripe is both a technology company and a financial services company. You will need to be comfortable straddling those worlds every day, moving quickly in the face of ambiguity to help scale our business globally. Responsibilities: You will be a critical team member responsible for:  Partner deeply with GTM and business teams for complex user deals to identify compliance roadblocks early and design the "path to yes" that aligns with our risk appetite. Lead compliance reviews and risk assessments for material user matters, providing clear, risk-based recommendations. Influence business roadmaps and design decisions, translating compliance requirements into clear, actionable product, control, and reporting expectations. Lead with a first-principles approach, bringing sound judgment to novel user-related questions and helping teams identify practical, sustainable paths forward. Deploy strategically as a subject matter expert to explain intricate compliance requirements to users and first line teams with authority, clarity, and empathy. Work with users and internal teams to architect solutions and flows that meet compliance obligations while minimizing friction. Work closely with Regional Compliance Officers, Money Laundering Reporting Officers, Legal, and other SMEs to support execution across complex, cross-functional user supportability designs. Help business teams build durable compliance capabilities by making established requirements, precedents, and standards easy to understand and apply independently, driving a “compliant by design” approach. Leverage AI and agentic tools to scale user enablement - including accelerating risk assessments, regulatory research, and requirements documentation - while applying rigorous judgment to novel, complex, or precedent-setting decisions and validating AI-generated outputs. Who you are Minimum Requirements 9+ years of experience building and managing compliance programs in regulated financial services, preferably in fintech, payments, or banking. Strong knowledge of regulatory compliance and financial crimes/AML practices, with an understanding of the risk landscape applicable to a company like Stripe. Proven ability to independently lead multiple complex projects and programs, from ambiguous early questions through implementation. Ability to interpret regulations and regulatory guidance, identify the underlying risks they are intended to address, and translate those requirements into comprehensive, proportionate compliance programs.
